text.p: French first division matches scheduled this Saturday (standings in parentheses, all kickoff times 1800 GMT):
Marseille (11) v Paris St Germain (2)

For security reasons there will be no PSG fans at Velodrome ground undergoing alterations for 1998 World Cup as police cannot guarantee being able to keep rival supporters apart. PSG midfielder Vincent Guerin and Marseille defender Hamada Jambay miss the game through suspension.
Nantes (3) v Montpellier (10)

Unbeaten in 29 matches, Nantes will be looking for PSG to slip up so they can snatch France's second European Cup berth. Montpellier, unbeaten in seven away games since mid-December, have Marseille-bound defender Serge Blanc and veteran Franck Sauzee doubtful with injuries.
Bastia (9) v Auxerre (6)

Outgoing champions, who cannot afford to lose if they are to stay in Europe next season, have tricky wing Bernard Diomede suspended. The Corsicans, beaten in last three games, have defender Sebastien Perez suspended and forward Wilfried Gohel injured.
Nice (20) v Metz (5)

Relegated Nice, looking to celebrate French Cup victory with a home win, will be without injured Italian playmaker Roberto Onorati but should have goalkeeper Bruno Valencony available despite a knock on the ankle. Metz, looking to ensure they play in next season's UEFA Cup, have midfielder Didier Lang suspended but keeper Lionel Letizi expected to return from injury.
Bordeaux (4) v Lyon (8)

Lyon, with six wins in last seven games, could upset Bordeaux side deprived through injury of full backs Patrick Colleter and Cyril Domoraud for this UEFA Cup "qualifier". But Lyon are without suspended striker Alain Caveglia.
Nancy (17) v Monaco (1)

If Monaco show championship-winning form they will condemn Nancy to relegation, but they have Victor Ikpeba suspended and goalkeeper Fabien Barthez, defenders Franck Dumas, Martin Djetou and Patrick Blondeau, midfielder John Collins and striker Anderson all out with injuries. Nancy striker Tony Cascarino is away on international duty with Ireland.
Strasbourg (7) v Lens (13)

Both teams will be relaxed, the home side because they are in the UEFA Cup as League Cup winners, Lens after ensuring they avoid relegation which until recently loomed large. Strasbourg's Czech defender Jan Suchoparek is suspended and Slovak goalkeeper Alexander Vencel still out with injury.
Caen (19) v Cannes (15)

Only victory might allow Caen to carry relegation fight to final day on May 24 if Rennes lose. They should beat a Cannes side decimated by injuries. Angry coach Guy Lacombe said: "I don't know how I'm going to name a side what with the injured and those who no longer want to play in the Lacombe era."
Rennes (16) v Guingamp (12)

Beaten at home only twice, Rennes can ensure top flight survival with victory, but Guingamp will look for performance to forget French Cup final disappointment. Guingamp are without keeper Angelo Hugues who has undergone cartilage surgery.
Lille (18) v Le Havre (14)

Lille, with only one point from last seven games, must win and hope Rennes lose if they are to retain any chance of staying in first division. Le Havre have midfielder Nicolas Huysman and defender Ludovic Pollet suspended.
